subject: general
question: The catalytic converter helps to convert unburnt hydrocarbons into:
solution:
The correct answer is __carbon dioxide and water.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Catalytic converter__ is a device used in vehicles to reduce harmful emissions.
 
• It converts unburnt hydrocarbons into carbon dioxide and water.
 
• The catalyst inside the converter facilitates chemical reactions without being consumed.
 
• This helps in reducing air pollution and is essential for meeting emission standards.
 
• Catalytic converters also help in converting carbon monoxide into less harmful carbon dioxide.
 
• They play a critical role in reducing smog-forming pollutants.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Carbon Monoxide:**

 
 
• A harmful gas produced by incomplete combustion of fuel.
 
• Catalytic converters reduce its emission significantly.
 
 
 
• **Nitrogen Oxides (NOx): **
 
 
• Formed at high temperatures in engine combustion chambers.
 
• These contribute to smog and acid rain.
 
• Catalytic converters help in reducing NOx emissions.
 
 
 
• **Water Vapor:**
 
 
• A byproduct of combustion and catalytic conversion.
 
• It is harmless and released into the atmosphere.
